name: Filter handoff
description: A sweep instead of a blend. A high-pass filter rises on the current song, draining away its bass and body until only a thin, bright edge is left, while the next song opens up from a muffled low-pass to full sound. Neither song is time-stretched, so it works even when the tempos do not match: the filters keep the two songs out of each other's way. A resonant peak on the sweep makes the movement audible; turn it down for a subtler handoff.
author: Muisc

sweepBars.label: Sweep length
sweepBars.doc: How many bars the sweep takes

hpfTo.label: Sweep top
hpfTo.doc: Where the high-pass on the old song ends; higher leaves less of it

q.label: Resonance
q.doc: How sharp the peak on the old song's sweep is (0.7 = none, 6 = whistling)

bLpfFrom.label: New song starts at
bLpfFrom.doc: Where the low-pass on the new song starts; lower is more muffled
